newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends higher on export sales, weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends higher on export sales, weather.

text.p: CBOT rice futures ended higher Thursday, boosted by weekly USDA export sales data that were above trade expectations and forecasts for cold, wet weather in the U.S. South, traders said.
"Export figures were better than expected," a trader said.
USDA on Thursday put export sales at 41,000 tonnes for the week ended April 3. That was well above trade expectations for 18,000 to 28,000 tonnes.
Weather continued to be a supportive factor. Forecasts called for a cold, wet weekend for much of the U.S. south, a primary rice growing region.
"The six- to 10-day looks like above normal rain and below normal temperatures across the belt," a trader said.
Rice closed nine to three cents higher, with May up nine at $11.36-1/2 per cwt.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 250 lots against Wednesday's actual volume of 282.
